pbg-artistoo — differential-adhesion cell rearrangement

Reproducing three simulations from the foundational Cellular Potts Model paper. Each is the real Artistoo simulator running in a Node.js subprocess, driven from Python via CPMSortingProcess — a two-type (light / dark) aggregate in a medium, with the paper's full cell-type adhesion matrix and area constraint. No motility: fluctuations come from finite-temperature Metropolis dynamics.

J. A. Glazier & F. Graner, “Simulation of the differential adhesion driven rearrangement of biological cells”, Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128 (1993).

Checkerboard (Fig. 7)Cell sorting / engulfment (Fig. 12)High-temperature mixing (Fig. 9 / Table II)

Checkerboard (Fig. 7)

Negative surface tension, γ_ld = −3

J_ll=10, J_dd=8, J_ld=6, J_lM=J_dM=12, T=10, λ=1. Because the heterotypic surface tension γ_ld is negative, unlike cells prefer to touch: light and dark cells intercalate and the heterotypic boundary fraction RISES toward a checkerboard. Here the two types are given DIFFERENT target areas through separate setpoint ports (large light 'gland' cells, small dark 'ciliated' cells — as in Honda's quail oviduct), so a sibling process could drive each type independently.

Cell sorting / engulfment (Fig. 12)

Technau–Holstein hydra energies, γ_ld = +3

J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=J_dM=16, T=10, λ=1. Cohesive dark cells (low J_dd) minimise their surface by clustering to the interior, engulfed by a light-cell monolayer. The heterotypic boundary fraction FALLS as the aggregate sorts.

High-temperature mixing (Fig. 9 / Table II)

Sorting energies at T = 40

The same cell-sorting energies, but T=40. Thermal fluctuations now exceed the surface-tension barriers, cell boundaries crumple, and the aggregate mixes rather than cleanly sorting — the paper's mixing transition (bulk moments blow up in Table II).
